about: Host indicators that vendors published for named macOS malware families, in the forms a process capture can show: code-signing team and signing IDs, file and plist paths, and strings in a command line. File hashes and network indicators beyond what appears in an argument are left out on purpose: a capture holds neither. Each entry names its source and how sure it is. high = read in the report's own page text, or quoted exactly in Objective-See's reproduction of it; medium = read only through a summarizing fetch, or from a single secondary page. Severity is high only for a high-confidence, distinctive indicator. An absence of matches proves nothing: indicators age, and a family changes its names between samples. Chollima names are CrowdStrike's: the cited reports say DPRK, Lazarus or BlueNoroff.
pathSyntax: `~/` is any user's home folder; `*` is any characters inside one path segment; `**/` is any number of folders; a trailing `/` means the folder and everything in it. Paths compare case-insensitively after /private/tmp, /private/var and /private/etc are written as /tmp, /var and /etc. kind `plist` is a launch plist file name, matched in /Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchDaemons and ~/Library/LaunchAgents. kind `argv` is a whole word in a command line, never argv[0].
